# Perform Breusch-Pagan test for heteroscedasticity

<small>Source: [`man/performBPTest.Rd`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/man/performBPTest.Rd) · Help: `?performBPTest`</small>

Implements the classical Breusch-Pagan (1979) test on a fitted linear model, in which the scaled squared residuals are regressed on the original regressors.

## Usage

```r
performBPTest(model, data = NULL)
performBreuschPaganTest(model, data = NULL)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   an object of class `lm`.

`data`
:   The data frame `model` was fitted to, or `NULL`, the default. The response, design, weights and offset are read from the fit itself, so a model that transforms its variables, has an `offset()` term, or takes its `weights` or `offset` from a column of the data needs no `data`, and the model frame of `model` is accepted as `data` (since 0.16.0; before, such models needed `data`). Data that are given are matched to the observations of the fit: rows with row names of their own by name, in any order; rows that only number themselves (a tibble, a data.table, a data frame whose row names were reset) by the row numbers of the fit, or in the order of the fit when they hold one row per observation. The rows the fit dropped may be there or not. Data whose rows cannot be shown to hold the observations of the fit are refused; see [`test_results`](test_results.md).

## Value

An object of class `htest` containing the test statistic, p-value and degrees of freedom.

## Details

The test statistic is half the explained sum of squares from regressing the scaled squared residuals \(e_i^2/\hat{\sigma}^2 - 1\) (with \(\hat{\sigma}^2 = \sum e_i^2 / n\)) on the explanatory variables. Under the null hypothesis of homoscedasticity *and normal disturbances* it follows a chi-square distribution whose degrees of freedom are the rank of the auxiliary regression less its intercept, the number of regressors on a model with an intercept (see *Degrees of freedom*), matching `lmtest::bptest(..., studentize = FALSE)`. For the studentized \(n R^2\) form that drops the normality assumption use [`performKoenkerTest`](performKoenkerTest.md).

The test is computed in memory whatever the size of the data. Up to 0.15.0 it switched to [`performBPTestStreaming()`](performBPTestStreaming.md) on data above 100 MB; call that function to stream.

## Degrees of freedom

The auxiliary regression of the scaled squared residuals on the regressors \(Z\) has an intercept, and the degrees of freedom are the rank of \([1, Z]\) minus one, the rank of the auxiliary regression less its intercept, as White's test counts them (see *Degrees of freedom* in [`performWhiteTest()`](performWhiteTest.md)) and as `lmtest::bptest()` does. A column of \(Z\) that is a linear combination of the intercept and the columns before it is dropped. So a model with an intercept counts its regressors, and a model without an intercept whose columns span the constant, such as the dummies of every level of a factor in `lm(y ~ 0 + group + x1)`, counts one fewer: the auxiliary regression adds an intercept that those columns already span. The rank is decided as in White's test, on the regressors centred one by one, at the default tolerance of [`qr()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/qr.html). A model whose only regressors are constant has none beyond the intercept, and is refused, as a model with an intercept alone is.

Up to 0.17.0 the degrees of freedom were the number of columns of \(Z\), one more on a model without an intercept whose columns span the constant, with the same statistic and a larger p-value: on `lm(y ~ 0 + group + x1)`, with a factor of four levels and 120 observations, 8.653 on 5 degrees of freedom (p = 0.124), where `lm(y ~ x1 + group)`, the same column space, and `lmtest::bptest(..., studentize = FALSE)` give 8.653 on 4 (p = 0.070), as the test now does. [`performBPTestStreaming()`](performBPTestStreaming.md) gives these degrees of freedom too, on such a model, which it refused up to 0.17.0 ("Breusch-Pagan auxiliary regression became rank deficient"), and so do [`performBPTestRobust()`](performBPTestRobust.md) with `studentize = FALSE`, whose interval follows them, and the registered `"breusch_pagan"` of [`runHeteroTests()`](runHeteroTests.md). A model with an intercept, or without one whose columns do not span the constant, such as `lm(y ~ 0 + x1 + x2)`, keeps its degrees of freedom. On the latter `lmtest::bptest()` given the model regresses the squared residuals on its columns without an intercept, and gives another statistic, as before; given the regressors as `varformula = ~ x1 + x2` it gives the value of this test.

Up to 0.17.0 the auxiliary regression was also fitted by `lm()` from a formula, on the columns of \(Z\) as they are, and on three kinds of design of full rank its statistic was wrong. It is now the value of [`performBPTestStreaming()`](performBPTestStreaming.md), which had it already, and of `lmtest::bptest()` but on the Gaussian `glm`, whose design `lmtest::bptest()` refits by `lm.fit()`, dropping the regressor too; [`performBPTestRobust()`](performBPTestRobust.md) with `studentize = FALSE` and the registered `"breusch_pagan"` change with it. On a model without an intercept with a regressor whose spread is less than about \(10^{-7}\) of its distance from zero, that fit dropped the regressor as a combination of its intercept, and the degrees of freedom still counted it: on the same 120 observations, `lm(y ~ 0 + I(x1 + 1e8) + x2)` gave 2.850 on 2 degrees of freedom (p = 0.241), where `lmtest::bptest()` given `varformula = ~ x1 + x2` and the test now give 16.72 (p = 0.0002). A Gaussian `glm`, fitted at a tolerance of \(10^{-11}\), keeps a regressor that `lm()` would alias: `glm(y ~ I(1e6 + x1 / 10) + x2)` gave 2.005 (p = 0.367) for 12.45 (p = 0.002), the value of `lm(y ~ x1 + x2)`, the same column space. And a regressor named `scaled_sq` was taken for the response of the formula: `lm(y ~ scaled_sq + x2)` gave 102.0 for 12.45, the value of the same model under another name. On other designs the statistic is the one it was.

## Exact fit

An auxiliary regression that fits the scaled squared residuals exactly has an \(R^2\) of 1, and the statistic, half its explained sum of squares, is half their total sum of squares, a function of the spread of the squared residuals alone, whatever their pattern. On a paired design, such as `lm(y ~ treat + subject)` with two observations of each subject, the two residuals of a subject sum to zero, so their squares are equal and a combination of the subject dummies: on 30 subjects the test gave 63.25 on 30 degrees of freedom (p = 0.0004) on homoscedastic data, the value of `lmtest::bptest(..., studentize = FALSE)`, and on `lm(y ~ x1 + f)` with a factor of 10 levels of two observations, 28.03 on 10 (p = 0.002). Since 0.18.0 it refuses such a regression when the design forces it, where it returned that statistic, as White's test refuses it (see *Too few observations* in [`performWhiteTest()`](performWhiteTest.md)). The refusal is an error of class `heteroTests_exact_fit_error`, whose message says why and asks for more observations per level: the design forces the exact fit, and more levels of two observations do not help. A fit counts as exact by the rule of White's test, when its residual sum of squares is at most `sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)`, about \(1.5 \times 10^{-8}\), of the total sum of squares of the squared residuals. The design forces it when the regression would fit the squares of the residuals of any response: the test pushes a fixed pseudo-response, standard normal draws from a fixed seed that leave the random numbers of the session as they were, through the QR decomposition of the fit, with its weights, and refuses only when the same regressors fit the squares of its residuals exactly too. A fit the data make exact is tested, as up to 0.17.0: in a one-way layout of nine groups of ten observations and one of two, with a value of the group of two typed 100 times too large, the dummies fit the squared residuals to within \(1.1 \times 10^{-9}\) of their total sum of squares, an exact fit by the rule, and the test gives 2069.35 on 9 degrees of freedom. A fit without a QR decomposition, such as an `mgcv::gam()` fit tested on its design, is refused, with a message that says only that the regression fits the squared residuals exactly.

[`performBPTestStreaming()`](performBPTestStreaming.md), the registered `"breusch_pagan"`, `performBreuschPaganTest()`, [`performBPTestRobust()`](performBPTestRobust.md) with `studentize = FALSE` and [`bootstrapTestStatistic()`](bootstrapTestStatistic.md) of this test refuse it too. [`runHeteroTests()`](runHeteroTests.md) takes no fallback, and stops with the refusal: of its fallbacks, Koenker's test fits the same squared residuals exactly, and the Cook-Weisberg test tests the fitted values, another hypothesis, and would return its value under this name. The other tests whose auxiliary regression can fit the squared residuals, or a function of them, exactly refuse such a fit by the same rule (see *Exact fit* in [`performKoenkerTest()`](performKoenkerTest.md)). [`autoTransform()`](autoTransform.md), which chooses a transformation by the p-value of this test, leaves out a candidate fit it refuses and stops with the refusal when every candidate is refused, as on such a design; on the one-way layout above it chooses `boxcox`, as up to 0.17.0.

The refusal covers the exact fit only. One step away from it, with one of the 30 subjects observed a third time, the test gives 64.74 on 30 (p = 0.0002), and on any fit with fixed effects for small groups it rejects too often, and warns (see *Fixed effects for small groups*).

## Fixed effects for small groups

The Breusch-Pagan test, like White's and Koenker's tests, is not valid with fixed effects for small groups: a factor with many levels and few observations of each, such as `subject` in `lm(y ~ x + subject)` with each subject observed a few times. On homoscedastic data, with normal errors, it rejects too often, and the more often the more levels the factor has and the fewer observations each level has. The excess comes from the dummies of the factor in the auxiliary regression. The residuals of a level are taken from its own mean, so under normal errors the squared residuals of a level of \(T\) observations vary between levels \(T / (T - 1)\) times as much as the auxiliary regression assumes, and with \(G\) levels the statistic exceeds its degrees of freedom by about \((G - 1) / (T - 1)\), as Koenker's did in the study below. Regressed on `x` alone, without the dummies, the squared residuals were rejected by this test in 4.3% to 5.6% of the draws (`inst/validation/fixed-effects-dummies.R`). The excess grows with \(G\) at a fixed \(T\), while the spread of the chi-squared distribution grows as \(\sqrt{2G}\), so with a fixed number of observations per level the size goes to 1 as the number of levels grows.

Since 0.16.0 the test warns when a term of the model that holds a factor or a character variable has more levels than observations per level: \(L > n / L\), that is \(L^2 > n\), with \(L\) the number of distinct combinations of the factors of the term among the \(n\) observations of the fit. The term is a factor, such as `subject`; an interaction of factors, counted by its cells, such as `a:b` of a crossed `a * b` or `school:class` of a nested `school / class`; or a slope for each level, `x:subject`. A variable left out of the formula, as in `y ~ . - id`, does not count. The warning names the term and gives \(L\), \(n\) and the mean number of observations per level; the statistic, the degrees of freedom and the p-value are those the test computes without it. It has class `heteroTests_fixed_effects_warning`, which `suppressWarnings(expr, classes = "heteroTests_fixed_effects_warning")` muffles, and no other warning. It is given on every call, also when [`cachedTest()`](cachedTest.md) or [`runHeteroTests()`](runHeteroTests.md) answers from its cache, and [`runHeteroTests()`](runHeteroTests.md) and [`runDiagnostics()`](runDiagnostics.md) give it once for each test that gives it. [`performBPTestStreaming()`](performBPTestStreaming.md), [`performBPTestRobust()`](performBPTestRobust.md) with `studentize = FALSE`, the deprecated `performBreuschPaganTest()` and the registered `"breusch_pagan"` give it too.

On a balanced design of \(G\) subjects of \(T\) observations the rule is \(G \le T\). In the study it kept the three tests within 2.5% to 7.5% at the 5% level where it holds, and put at least one of them outside where it does not, in 68 of the 69 designs where they computed; the exception is this test on 20 subjects of 20, at 8.0%. Unbalanced groups, a second regressor and a regressor correlated with the subject effects followed the same pattern, with the mean number of observations per level, \(n / G\), in place of \(T\). The rule is a warning, not a correction, and many panels fail it: on 100 firms observed over 10 years the three tests reject in 18% to 21% of the draws. Rejection at the 5% level, in percent, in 2,000 homoscedastic draws of `lm(y ~ x + subject)`, with `x`, the subject effects and the errors standard normal:

rrrrrl
Subjects  Observations of each  White  Koenker  Breusch-Pagan  Warns

10  10  6.4  6.2  7.3  no

20  20  6.0  6.4  8.0  no

5  4  1.0  5.4  7.0  yes

30  3  50.7  57.3  39.6  yes

30  4  22.2  23.9  28.7  yes

100  8  23.8  23.8  25.2  yes

100  10  18.1  18.4  21.3  yes

200  4  97.8  97.6  82.5  yes

A slope for each level counts too, but there the error goes the other way: with a slope for each subject, `lm(y ~ x + x:subject)`, on 30 subjects of 3 and of 4 and on 100 of 8, the three tests rejected too rarely, White's in 0.7% to 2.2% of the draws, Koenker's in 0.1% to 0.8% and the Breusch-Pagan test in 0.4% to 2.8% (`inst/validation/fixed-effects-variants-size.R`). The warning therefore says that the p-value is unreliable: in the simulations usually far too small, and too large with a slope per level.

The study is `inst/validation/fixed-effects-size.R`, with its results in `fixed-effects-size.csv` (`system.file("validation", package = "heteroTests")`). Juhl and Sosa-Escudero (2014) derive a test of heteroskedasticity for this setting, after fixed effects estimation of a panel of many units observed a fixed number of times; it needs to be told which factor is the unit, and the package does not implement it.

## Deprecated name

`performBreuschPaganTest()` is deprecated since 0.14.0. It was the same function as `performBPTest()` under a second name; it still works, returns what `performBPTest()` returns and warns. Use `performBPTest()`.

## Weighted fits

On a fit with weights the test is computed from the Pearson residuals \(\sqrt{w_i}\, e_i\), so it tests whether the weights are adequate; see the section on weighted fits in [`performKoenkerTest()`](performKoenkerTest.md), which also covers weights estimated by [`fitWLS()`](fitWLS.md).

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link, unweighted
or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a rank-deficient fit, which it
tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the same model fitted without the
aliased columns. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a `survey::svyglm()` fit, a
fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another reason, and `data` that
lack rows or variables of the fit. Which model each test accepts, and why, is set out in
[`test_results`](test_results.md), under *Supported models*.

## References

Breusch, T. S., & Pagan, A. R. (1979). A simple test for heteroscedasticity and random coefficient variation. *Econometrica*, 47(5), 1287–1294. [doi:10.2307/1911963](https://doi.org/10.2307/1911963)

Koenker, R. (1981). A note on studentizing a test for heteroscedasticity. *Journal of Econometrics*, 17(1), 107–112. [doi:10.1016/0304-4076(81)90062-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/0304-4076%2881%2990062-2)

Juhl, T., & Sosa-Escudero, W. (2014). Testing for heteroskedasticity in fixed effects models. *Journal of Econometrics*, 178(Part 3), 484–494. [doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2013.07.005](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jeconom.2013.07.005)

## Examples

```r
 data(mtcars)
 m <- lm(mpg ~ wt + qsec, data = mtcars)
 performBPTest(m, mtcars)
```
